evidence: Ter. Haut. 1065: Nunc laudō tē, gnāte.
terms.comment: Laudō alone is also ‘well done!’ (Eu noster! laudō., Ter. Eun. 154; see well done). To praise God is Deum laudāre: Laudāte, puerī, Dominum (Ps. 112 (113), 1).
Praise, and the good name it brings.

evidence: Plaut. Capt. 420–421: suom erum servos collaudāvit

phrases.latin: lūsus hic sit; et rogētur et laudētur et numquam nōn fēcisse sē gaudeat
phrases.english: let it be a game; let him be asked questions and praised, and always be glad he did it

phrases.latin: mihi ille dētur puer, quem laus excitet, quem glōria juvet, quī victus fleat
phrases.english: give me the boy whom praise spurs on, who loves glory, who cries when he loses
Now I’m proud of you, my son.
